dedupe_keys.name: caltrans active transportation count dataset pedestrian and bicycle counts on state highways

description: The Active Transportation Count Dataset from the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) documents non-motorised traffic on state highways. It grew out of district pilots started in 2023 to monitor active transportation: vendors collect the counts with technologies such as video analytics and share them with Caltrans headquarters through APIs or files, where they are standardised statewide. Coverage: count sites on the California state highway system, with hourly pedestrian and bicycle volumes by site and direction; separate pedestrian and bicycle files are published for 2023 and 2024. Core fields are a site identifier, date and hour, direction, count and latitude and longitude. Format and access: CSV files on the California open data portal, with a data dictionary, metadata workbook, labelling conventions and a data quality management plan. Licence and cost: free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: Caltrans notes possible undercounts in adverse weather and incomplete coverage while the pilots expand. The counts can be used to calibrate pedestrian and cycling flows in network flow models of state highway corridors and to test safety or Complete Streets scenarios. It relates to the Caltrans Transportation Equity Index and the York cycle counters in the catalogue.
